sections.markdown:
# Graduated licensing, tests, records and litter responsibility

FACT_ID: sec02-R01 | anchor: A01
The guide states that a driver license expires six years from the nearest birthday. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec02-R02 | anchor: A01
Renewal may be requested during the 180 days before license expiration. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec02-R03 | anchor: A01
A vision examination is required before a driver license is renewed. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec02-R04 | anchor: A01
A newly issued license should be checked for correct information before leaving the office. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec02-R05 | anchor: A01
The guide says immigration status may cause a different expiration date for an immigrant, nonimmigrant or refugee. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec02-R06 | anchor: A01
For qualifying service outside Louisiana, an Armed Forces or Peace Corps member’s license and qualifying dependents’ licenses remain valid for sixty days after discharge if valid on entering service. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec02-R07 | anchor: A01
Under that service rule, the license becomes expired or delinquent on the sixty-first day after discharge. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec02-R08 | anchor: A01
The last license and proof of discharge are accepted for renewal under the service-extension rule. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec02-R09 | anchor: A01
A Louisiana resident younger than seventy with a Class D or E license may be selected for mail or internet renewal. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec02-R10 | anchor: A01
Mail or internet renewal invitations are not issued for two consecutive renewal cycles. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec02-R11 | anchor: A01
A driver who is offered mail or internet renewal may instead renew in person. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec02-R12 | anchor: A01
A driver must update the address on a Louisiana license within ten days after moving. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec02-R13 | anchor: A02
A license name change may be supported by a certified marriage license, a certified birth certificate for return to the birth name, or a certified court order authorizing the change. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec02-R14 | anchor: A02
A name change between renewals incurs a duplicate-license fee. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec02-R15 | anchor: A02
A lost, stolen or destroyed license may be replaced by applying in person at a motor-vehicle office. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec02-R16 | anchor: A02
For a minor’s duplicate license, a custodial or domiciliary parent, tutor or legal guardian must appear with identification and custody documents to sign; with joint custody, only the domiciliary parent may sign. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec02-R17 | anchor: A02
A duplicate-license applicant must provide current liability-insurance proof for any registered vehicle. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec02-R18 | anchor: A02
OMV or a court may impose driving restrictions that appear on the license. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec02-R19 | anchor: A02
Violating a license restriction breaks the law and can cause suspension of driving privileges. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec02-R20 | anchor: A02
The guide requires a detailed physician or vision-specialist report for a physically impaired first-time applicant or a first-time applicant older than sixty. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec02-R21 | anchor: A02
The required medical-report form must be obtained from OMV and must describe conditions that could impair safe driving. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec02-R22 | anchor: A02
OMV may require anyone to provide a medical or vision report and may also require written or road-skills testing. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec02-R23 | anchor: A02
OMV keeps public records of traffic convictions and collisions for five years, while DWI convictions remain for ten years, including convictions received in other states. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec02-R24 | anchor: A02
A Louisiana identification card proves identity but does not authorize driving. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec02-R25 | anchor: A02
An identification-card applicant must meet the identification requirements and have a valid Louisiana residential address. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec02-R26 | anchor: A02
The guide lists a revoked license, unfinished required driver training, unpassed required tests and age below fifteen as reasons a person is ineligible for a driver license. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec02-R27 | anchor: A03
Altering license information, using a license unlawfully, or falsifying or hiding a material application fact can result in losing driving privileges. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0017]

sections.heading: Graduated licensing, tests, records and litter responsibility
sections.markdown:
# Graduated licensing, tests, records and litter responsibility

FACT_ID: sec02-R28 | anchor: A03
Failing to stop and assist after a collision involving injury or death can result in loss of driving privileges. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-R29 | anchor: A03
A DWI conviction or refusal of an alcohol-analysis test after a DWI arrest can result in losing driving privileges. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-R30 | anchor: A03
The guide lists an alcohol-test result of at least 0.08 percent for a driver twenty-one or older, or at least 0.02 percent for a driver younger than twenty-one, as grounds for losing driving privileges. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-R31 | anchor: A03
Failing to stop for a school bus while children are loading or unloading can result in loss of driving privileges. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-R32 | anchor: A03
Vehicle-related manslaughter, negligent homicide or another felony committed while operating a vehicle can result in loss of driving privileges. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-R33 | anchor: A03
Three reckless-driving convictions within twelve months can result in losing driving privileges. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-R34 | anchor: A03
Unanswered traffic charges, violation of a license restriction, failure to meet financial-responsibility requirements or driving while suspended can result in loss of driving privileges. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-R35 | anchor: A03
An out-of-state offense can affect Louisiana driving privileges when the same offense would support suspension or revocation in Louisiana. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-R36 | anchor: A03
The guide lists unpaid child support or state income taxes as possible grounds for losing driving privileges. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-R37 | anchor: A03
Leaving school before graduation while aged fifteen through seventeen, or being found habitually absent or tardy, can affect driving privileges. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-R38 | anchor: A04
Littering includes improperly leaving or discarding waste whether intentionally or unintentionally. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-R39 | anchor: A04
The guide distinguishes accidental simple littering, deliberate intentional littering and gross littering involving large amounts of waste or an illegal dump. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-R40 | anchor: A04
Unsecured loads can shed objects that cause collisions, delays, injuries or deaths. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-R41 | anchor: A04
The guide attributes more than 143.8 million Louisiana roadside litter pieces to a 2023 Keep Louisiana Beautiful study. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-R42 | anchor: A04
The guide attributes more than seventy-nine percent of Louisiana roadside litter to motorists, pickup trucks, garbage trucks and unsecured loads. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-R43 | anchor: A04
Cigarette butts are identified as the most littered small item and plastic water bottles as the most visible littered roadside item in the guide’s cited study. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-R44 | anchor: A04
The cited study found more than 61.9 million roadside plastic items, with plastic water bottles present at eighty percent of surveyed sites. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-R45 | anchor: A04
The guide states that wind and rain move light roadside waste into waterways and that eighty percent of land litter eventually reaches a waterway. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-R46 | anchor: A04
The guide explains that cigarette litter releases pollutants in water, may be eaten by wildlife, and has caused wildfires on land. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-R47 | anchor: A05
Accidental and deliberate littering are both unlawful and can lead to civil or criminal proceedings. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec02-R48 | anchor: A05
For simple littering, the guide lists a first-offense penalty of a 150-dollar fine or eight community-service hours, rising for a second offense to 900 dollars or twenty community-service hours. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec02-R49 | anchor: A05
A driver is responsible for litter leaving the vehicle or truck bed, including litter discarded by passengers. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec02-R50 | anchor: A05
A loaded truck bed must be covered or secured so cargo and debris do not fall out. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec02-R51 | anchor: A05
A litter report should record the vehicle description and plate, plus the incident’s date, time and location, and the call should be made while parked. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec02-R52 | anchor: A05
The guide reports 91.4 million dollars in annual Louisiana litter cleanup and prevention spending. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec02-R53 | anchor: A05
The guide links litter with reduced property values, weaker business and tourism activity, blocked drainage, flooding risk, harm to wildlife and reduced quality of life. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec02-R54 | anchor: A05
Prevent litter by containing vehicle trash until it can be placed in a receptacle, requiring passengers not to litter, and keeping loose items from escaping a truck bed. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec02-R55 | anchor: A05
A smoker can keep a portable ashtray in the vehicle rather than discard cigarette butts through a window. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0019]
